Samantha - thanks, great questions. Quick answers below and Marissa will follow up with formalized language where needed.

- Controller vs Processor: Redwood's default stance is that customers (Stellar) are the controller of customer data they send for processing (including PII and embeddings). Redwood acts as a processor. Model outputs are treated as derived data; we do not claim ownership. We will add language to the DPA to explicitly state this mapping for inference and embedding use cases.

- Subprocessors: Attached is the current subprocessors list in the DPA appendix. Short answer: we use cloud providers (AWS us-east-1 primary), a managed logging provider for aggregated telemetry (no access to plaintext request bodies by default), and a managed billing provider. We can provide a full list and confirm which subprocessors have potential access to unredacted data under strict contractual controls.

- Breach notice: Redwood's policy is to provide initial notification within 72 hours of confirmed detection. For suspected incidents we typically notify as soon as we have actionable information; we'll commit to 72 hours for confirmed breaches in the DPA. Post-notification we provide a timeline for remediation steps and root cause analysis.

- Data residency: We support region-scoped projects for both POC and production. For Stellar we can pin the project to US-only regions (us-east-1 or us-west-2) so embeddings/requests and backups remain in the US. We'll note options for customer-controlled key management (bring-your-own-key) if required.

Next steps: 
- Marissa: can you confirm the precise DPA wording for controller/processor and the 72-hour breach SLA so Jonas can share a revised DPA?
- Samantha / Amit: send any specific redlines or clauses you need on subprocessors/data residency and we'll prioritize.

Happy to jump on Thu morning PT.

Best,
Jonas

Hi Samantha / Amit -

Looping in formally from Legal. Thanks for the clear asks - below are the proposed clarifications we can commit to in Redwood_DPA_v2 (we can produce a redline if helpful):

1) Controller/Processor: we will add a clause that expressly states: "Customer (Stellar Finance) is the Controller of Customer Data submitted to Redwood for processing; Redwood Inference acts as Processor. Customer retains all rights and responsibilities as Controller, including lawful basis for processing and notices to data subjects."

2) Subprocessors: we will provide a complete list of current subprocessors in an appendix and commit to notify customers of new subprocessors 30 days in advance with an opt-out / termination right where local law requires. Subprocessors with potential access to unredacted data are limited to our cloud provider in the selected US region and an audited logging provider; both are contractually bound to our terms and SOC2 controls.

3) Breach Notice: we propose language committing to initial notification within 72 hours of confirmed detection and best-effort immediate notification for suspected incidents. We will include escalation contacts and a post-incident remediation/forensics timeline in the appendix.

4) Data Residency & Retention: we will include an option to pin data to US-only regions for the POC and production; retention defaults to 30 days for request bodies/KV cache unless customer requests a shorter/longer retention and can configure retention via the Console or via an API. We will document encryption at rest, in transit, and BYOK options for KMS.

If that mapping works, Jonas will incorporate the redline and I can run a final review. Happy to set a short call with your legal team to walk through the exact wording.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
